security_audit.summary: The two external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and a fenced URL block; neither executes a shell command. The skill intentionally fetches mutable remote instructions, creating a network dependency and an indirect prompt-injection or supply-chain risk.

remediation.issue: Remote rules are fetched from a mutable branch and treated as instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the source to an immutable commit, verify its hash, and treat fetched text as untrusted reference data rather than agent instructions.

static_findings.snippet: 4. Output findings in the terse `file:line` format

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks only format the literal file:line output convention in Markdown. No shell or Ruby execution is present.
Line 25 is a Markdown fence that begins a plain URL block. It does not invoke a shell, Ruby, or any executable command.
The skill explicitly requires fetching this URL before every review, so network access is intentional. The mutable remote document is then treated as review instructions.

content.user_title: Audit Web Interfaces Against Current Guidelines
content.value_statement: Interface reviews often miss accessibility, usability, and consistency problems. This skill fetches current Web Interface Guidelines and reports code findings with file and line references.
actual_capabilities: Fetches the latest Web Interface Guidelines from its configured public source before each review.
Reads user-specified files or file patterns and asks for scope when none is provided.
Evaluates interface code against all rules contained in the fetched guidelines.
Reports findings using concise file and line references.
Supports accessibility, UX, design, and interface best-practice review requests.
limitations: Requires network access to retrieve the latest guidelines.
Depends on a mutable external document, so review criteria can change without a skill update.
Reviews only available source files and does not automatically test rendered interfaces in a browser.
Reports issues but does not automatically modify affected files.

use_cases.title: Review a feature before merge
use_cases.description: Audit changed interface files for guideline violations before submitting a pull request.

use_cases.title: Check accessibility implementation
use_cases.description: Inspect form, navigation, and interaction code for accessibility concerns covered by current guidelines.

use_cases.title: Validate design system adoption
use_cases.description: Review product interface files for consistency, usability, and implementation quality.

prompt_templates.title: Review one interface file
prompt_templates.prompt: Review {file} against the current Web Interface Guidelines. Report each issue with its file and line number.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a focused review of one file.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a component folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit files matching {pattern}. Focus on accessibility, interaction behavior, responsive layout, and visual consistency.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants to review a related component set.

prompt_templates.title: Review a user flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review {files} for the {user_flow} journey. Prioritize blockers, accessibility failures, confusing interactions, and inconsistent states.
prompt_templates.scenario: A product team wants findings organized around a workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Run a release readiness audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit {scope} against all current guidelines. Group findings by severity, cite exact locations, identify repeated patterns, and summarize release risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced team needs a broad pre-release interface assessment.

output_examples.input: Review the checkout form for accessibility and interaction issues.
output: checkout-form.html:42 - The input has no associated label.
checkout-form.css:118 - Focus styling is removed without a visible replacement.

output_examples.input: Audit the navigation components for responsive behavior.
output: navigation.tsx:67 - The menu control does not expose its expanded state.
navigation.css:91 - The mobile menu can extend beyond the viewport.

output_examples.input: Review the settings page against all current guidelines.
output_examples.output: settings-page.tsx:134 - The destructive action lacks a clear confirmation step.

best_practices: Provide exact files or a narrow pattern so findings remain relevant and traceable.
Include the interface purpose and important user flows when requesting a review.
Re-run audits when upstream guidelines or reviewed interface code changes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat source review as a replacement for browser, keyboard, or assistive-technology testing.
Do not submit broad repository patterns when only one interface area needs review.
Do not accept fetched instructions without considering source integrity and unexpected changes.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews specified interface source files against rules fetched from the configured Web Interface Guidelines source.

faq.question: Does it check accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It reports accessibility concerns covered by the fetched guidelines, but it does not replace manual testing.

faq.question: Can it review multiple files?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a file pattern or an explicit list of files to define the scope.

faq.question: Does it fix reported issues?
faq.answer: No. The skill reports findings and locations but does not automatically edit files.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. It fetches the latest guideline document from a public GitHub URL before each review.

faq.question: Can review results change over time?
faq.answer: Yes. The remote guidelines are mutable, so new upstream rules can change findings without a local skill update.
